Know the definition of an employer and what an employer’s obligations are under the CPF Act.

Under the CPF Act, an employer is defined as:

• Any person, company, association, or body of persons, whether or not incorporated, by whom an employee is employed;

• The owners of any vessel on which an employee is employed; or

• Any manager, agent, or person responsible for the payment of wages to an employee, on behalf of an employer.

As an employer, you’re required to pay CPF contributions for your employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents and who are earning total wages of more than $50 per month.

You need to pay total CPF contributions (comprising of the employer and employee’s shares) to the CPF Board. You’re entitled to recover the employee’s share of CPF contributions when paying your employee’s wages for the month.

Note: If your employee earns above $50 but not more than $500 per month, there is no employee’s share of CPF contributions. You will still need to pay the employer's share of CPF contributions.

You need to have a CSN to submit CPF contributions. Don’t have a CSN? Apply for a CSN by logging in with your Singpass.

Understand why you need to declare accurate wage information for your employees when submitting CPF contributions.

Wages determine the amount of CPF contributions employers must make. It is important to declare accurate wage information to CPF Board so that the correct amount of CPF contribution can be verified.

Learn how to compute and when to submit CPF contributions.

Determine who your employees are. Know who are entitled to CPF contributions.

CPF contributions are payable on wages. Learn which payments are considered wages and how to classify them as Ordinary Wages or Additional Wages.

The CPF contribution rate applicable depends on whether employee is a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident, age, and total wages.

The due date for CPF contributions is on the last day of the calendar month. Enforcement action would be taken against employers who fail to pay by the 14th of the following month.

Learn more about the common mistakes you should avoid when making CPF contributions.

There are several easy ways you can pay CPF contributions.

Find out about other payments that can be submitted together with CPF contributions.

SDL is a compulsory levy that you have to pay for all your employees working in Singapore, on top of CPF contributions.

The SHGs are set up to uplift the less privileged and low income households in the Chinese, Eurasian, Muslim, and Indian communities. Employers are expected to deduct SHG contributions from their employees’ wages.

SGSHARE is the national regular-giving programme that supports communities in need. It is an initiative by Community Chest, the philanthropic arm of the National Council of Social Service.

Are you an employer or insurer with a contractual obligation to reimburse your employee or insured’s medical expenses? Learn how you can perform these reimbursements electronically.

The owners of any vessel on which an employee is employed; or

Any manager, agent, or person responsible for the payment of wages to an employee, on behalf of an employer.

Obligations of an employer

As an employer, you’re required to pay CPF contributions for your employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents and who are earning total wages of more than $50 per month.

Note: If your employee earns above $50 but not more than $500 per month, there is no employee’s share of CPF contributions. You will still need to pay the employer's share of CPF contributions.
